claim.quote: This cumulative exposure (107731 kg day) has given a model independent evidence for the presence of a Dark Matter particle component in the galactic halo at 6.3 sigma C.L.; this main result is summarised here.

key_value.note: Cumulative exposure of the seven annual cycles.

name: Results from DAMA/NaI and perspectives for DAMA/LIBRA
notes: Conference summary of the same data set as result:dama-nai-seven-annual-cycles-2003; kept because its abstract uses the word 'evidence'.

summary.plain: A short summary by the DAMA team of its seven-year sodium iodide data, which it says gives model-independent evidence for dark matter in the galaxy's halo at 6.3 standard deviations. The same paper announces the larger DAMA/LIBRA detector, which started taking data in March 2003.
summary.technical: Conference summary of the DAMA/NaI final result (seven annual cycles, 107731 kg day): 'model independent evidence' at 6.3 sigma C.L.; also reports that DAMA/LIBRA (about 250 kg NaI(Tl)) is taking data since March 2003.

title: Results from DAMA/NaI and perspectives for DAMA/LIBRA
why_it_matters: Records the claim in the collaboration's own wording ('evidence'); it summarises the same data set as the review-article record.
